examples.knowledge_point: Integrating Rational Functions With Repeated Factors of Degree Two
examples.worked_solution:
First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\dfrac{2x+3}{(x+1)^2} = \dfrac{A}{(x+1)} +\dfrac{B}{(x+1)^2}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ and $B,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x+1)^2$ and get

$$
2x+3 = A(x+1)+B .
$$

Plugging in $x=-1,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-1)+3 & =A(-1+1)+B \\ 1 & =0+B \\ B & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $B,$ we can solve for $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(0)+3 & =A(0+1)+B \\ 3 & =A+B \\ 3 & =A+1 \\ A & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\dfrac{2x+3}{(x+1)^2} = \dfrac{2}{(x+1)} +\dfrac{1}{(x+1)^2}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{2x+3}{(x+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{2}{(x+1)}+\frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1||}_{0}^{1}+{(-\frac{1}{x+1})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2{\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1||}_{0}^{1}-{\frac{1}{x+1}|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2[\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1]-[\frac{1}{2}-1] \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
